Chan Buddhism.fact: In Chan, the usage of esoteric mantras goes back to the Tang dynasty. Influential esoteric dhāraṇī, such as the Uṣṇīṣa Vijaya Dhāraṇī Sūtra and the Nīlakaṇṭha Dhāraṇī, also begin to be cited in the literature of the Baotang school during the Tang dynasty.

Chan Buddhism.fact: There is evidence that Chan Buddhists adopted practices from Chinese Esoteric Buddhism in findings from Dunhuang.

Many mantras have been preserved since the Tang period and continue to be practiced in modern monasteries.

Chan Buddhism.subject: Indian Society
Chan Buddhism.question: One common example is the Śūraṅgama _____, which is commonly chanted by monastics as part of the morning liturgy (朝誦 Chaosong) and evening liturgy (暮誦 Musong) in temples
Chan Buddhism.fact: The eighth century Chan monks of Shaolin temple also performed esoteric practices such as mantras and dharanis. Many mantras have been preserved since the Tang period and continue to be practiced in modern monasteries.

Chan Buddhism.subject: Indian Society
Chan Buddhism.question: The Chinese Chan master _____ (720–814 CE) left behind a famous saying which had been the guiding principle of his life, "A day without work is a day without food"
Chan Buddhism.fact: The Chinese Chan master Baizhang (720–814 CE) left behind a famous saying which had been the guiding principle of his life, "A day without work is a day without food".

Chan Buddhism.question: These included food gardening or farming, carpentry, architecture, housekeeping, administration (or community direction), and the practice of _____ medicine
Chan Buddhism.fact: These included food gardening or farming, carpentry, architecture, housekeeping, administration (or community direction), and the practice of Traditional Chinese medicine.
